small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=1024, N=8192, K=8192 — large K dominates. Add larger-K autotune configs (BLOCK_K=64, 128) and BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256 with num_warps=8, num_stages=4 to better overlap K-loop loads. Also add a GROUP_M=8 swizzle on the (pid_m, pid_n) grid for L2 reuse across the 64 N-tiles per M-row.
- Transpose W once at init (store W^T as (K, N) contiguous) so the inner-K load of B is contiguous along K with stride 1, eliminating the strided wn-major load in the hot loop.
- Fuse softmax into the GEMM epilogue when N fits a single program: since N=8192 fits in a persistent row kernel, use one program per M row that streams K-blocks for the full row, computes max+sumexp online, and writes softmax — removes the 2 extra full-tensor passes. Alternatively, in the current 2-kernel design, raise softmax BLOCK_N to 2048 or 4096 with num_warps=8 to halve the number of N-loop iterations.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a fused GEMM→BN-affine→scale→softmax kernel with one program per output row (M=1024 rows, plenty of parallelism). Each program tiles K in BLOCK_K chunks, accumulates the full N=8192 row into registers/SRAM tile-by-tile along N, then in the same kernel does the online softmax (running max + sumexp) and final normalize+store. This eliminates the intermediate (M,N)=1024×8192 write+read between GEMM and softmax (~32MB each direction).
- If a single program per row is too register-heavy, use a split-N persistent strategy: each program owns a (row, N-tile) and accumulates the GEMM, then a second small kernel does row-wise softmax across N-tiles via atomics or a 2-pass reduction over the already-resident tile buffer in shared memory.
- Consider using tensor-core friendly fp16/bf16 accumulation for the GEMM with fp32 accumulator — the RTX 4090 has very high TC throughput; cast x and W^T to bf16 at init time (weight) and per-call (input) to roughly 2× the GEMM throughput, then keep epilogue in fp32 for numerical stability of softmax.
